## Analysis

**Test image observations:**
- Cross-section of a corn ear viewed from one end
- White cottony mold filling the center (cob/silk channel area)
- Kernels are pale/grayish with pinkish-reddish discoloration — not healthy yellow
- Silks visible, suggesting the tip end
- Overall bleached/grayish kernel appearance with some reddish tints

**Reference comparison:**
- **Fusarium**: White to salmon-colored cottony mold, typically on scattered/insect-damaged kernels on otherwise yellow corn. Starburst pattern on individual kernels. The mold in the test image is more centralized.
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pinkish-red mold entering via silk channel at tip. References show very dark pink-red colored ears — more intense than the test image. However, early stage is "pinkish-white," which could match.
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold starting at base, grayish-brown mummified kernels. The Diplodia reference close-up panels show grayish/pale kernels densely packed with white surface coating — this matches the test image kernel appearance well.
- **Aspergillus/Trichoderma**: Ruled out — no olive-green or dark green mold present.
- **Common_smut**: Ruled out — no large fleshy galls.

**Decision:** The pale/grayish mummified-looking kernels with white mold and some pinkish tints, viewed in cross-section, most closely match **Fusarium** ear rot — the white cottony mold with pink/reddish kernel discoloration is characteristic. However, the central location of the mold (near the silk channel at the tip) and pinkish kernel streaking also fit **Ear_rots_Gibberella**. The kernels' grayish bleached color and white central mold tips the balance slightly toward Fusarium.
